intro: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, then added Sheets, Whiteboards, Claude Data, Claude Meetings and self-hosted Managed Agents in the same week. Google answered with Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Jensen Huang resigned as NVIDIA CEO, and AWS made its local AWS Emulator public.

top.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
top.body: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 (claude-fable-5-2) and Claude Mythos 5.2 on November 9. Both have a 1M-token context window, 128k max output and always-on adaptive thinking.

top.title: Jensen Huang resigns as NVIDIA CEO; CFO Colette Kress steps in
top.body: NVIDIA's board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation on November 11 and the company confirmed it on November 12. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and stays CFO, and Harvey Jones became NVIDIA's first board chair.

top.title: Google makes Gemini 4 Carbon generally available
top.body: Gemini 4 Carbon is now on the paid Gemini API, Gemini for business, Antigravity and for Google AI Ultra subscribers. The introductory price is $2 input and $10 output per million tokens; from November 30 it is $4/$20.

top.title: Anthropic adds Claude Sheets, Whiteboards, Claude Data and interactive connectors
top.body: Anthropic launched Claude Sheets for shared spreadsheets with formulas and tabs, and Claude Whiteboards for meetings. Claude Data (formerly Dashboards) connects to Snowflake and Salesforce to build dashboards and data stories.

top.title: Anthropic lets enterprises self-host the full Claude Managed Agents service
top.body: Anthropic launched self-hosted Claude Managed Agents on November 12. Customers can run the whole Managed Agents service on their own infrastructure, not only the sandboxes, and store agents, sessions and session history there.

top.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast 1M-context model
top.body: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12. It has a 1M-token input window and up to 1M output tokens, with flat pricing of $1.50 per million input and $7.50 per million output tokens.

top.title: AWS Emulator runs AWS APIs locally for tests and CI
top.body: AWS Emulator serves AWS API endpoints on your machine, a dev server or in CI. It runs as a Linux package, in Docker on Windows and macOS, or embedded in Rust tests.

top.title: DeepMind's AlphaProof Code formally verifies Signal's cryptographic code
top.body: AlphaProof Code is a multi-agent framework where humans choose what to prove and agents write Lean proofs. The team verified core cryptographic code of the Signal protocol down to compiled machine code in four weeks.

top.title: Cursor incident exposed tampered Claude Code extension builds
top.body: Cursor published an update on its 29 October security incident, which started with a storage key exposed at Fireworks. Tampered anthropic.claude-code extension builds 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 stayed cached for about 11 hours and reached at most 5,000 users.

top.title: Claude Meetings enters beta on Google Meet
top.body: Anthropic brought Claude into live meetings with Claude Meetings. It is in beta for Team and Enterprise users and starts on Google Meet.

models.name: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
models.what: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 (claude-fable-5-2) and Claude Mythos 5.2 on November 9.

models.name: Muse Ember
models.what: Meta released Muse Ember, its smallest and most efficient Muse model, on November 9.

models.name: Gemini 4 Carbon
models.what: Gemini 4 Carbon is now on the paid Gemini API, Gemini for business, Antigravity and for Google AI Ultra subscribers.

models.name: Gemini Robotics 2.5
models.what: Gemini Robotics 2.5 is DeepMind's new vision-language-action model, tested on more than 200 tasks.

models.name: Alpamayo 2 Edge
models.what: NVIDIA announced Alpamayo 2 Edge, which brings adaptive AI reasoning to the vehicle in real time.

models.name: Strands Decider
models.what: Amazon used Strands Decider, an open-source decision model on Gemma 4 E4B, to label tickets instead of Claude Sonnet 4.6.

models.name: Gemini Decision 1
models.what: Gemini Decision 1 (gemini-decision-1) scores up to 1,000 closed-set questions in one forward pass instead of generating text.

models.name: Qwen4-Max Preview
models.what: Alibaba opened a Qwen4-Max preview on 11 November that runs until 25 November 2026.

models.name: H3-Image
models.what: MiniMax released H3-Image with downloadable model weights.

models.name: Gemini 4 Hydrogen
models.what: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12.

models.name: Edge0-145B
models.what: Edge0 released Edge0-145B, a sparse mixture-of-experts model with 145B total and about 10B active parameters, plus Edge0-120B.

models.name: Granite 4.1 LLMON
models.what: IBM released experimental 3B and 8B Granite 4.1 LLMON previews.

models.name: Inkling 2 Small (open weights)
models.what: Thinking Machines Lab made the Inkling 2 Small weights downloadable on Hugging Face after safety testing.

chips.title: Google unveils TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max
chips.body: TPU 8i Max puts two TPU 8i chips in one package with 384 GB HBM, 17.2 TB/s HBM bandwidth and 768 MB SRAM, double the bandwidth and compute of one TPU 8i.

chips.title: AMD Instinct MI430X: 432 GB HBM4 for exascale AI and HPC
chips.body: MI430X uses the CDNA 5 architecture with 432 GB of HBM4 at up to 23.3 TB/s.

chips.title: NVIDIA serves 753B GLM-5.3 across two DGX Stations
chips.body: NVIDIA served GLM-5.3 NVFP4 (753B total, 40B active parameters, about 464 GB) across two DGX Stations with GB300 GPUs linked by ConnectX-8 RDMA.

skill_of_week.name: janestreet/agent_skills: Socratic Tutor
skill_of_week.what: Jane Street's first public agent skill turns a coding agent or chatbot into a strict personal tutor. It starts with a diagnostic, builds a skill map that rates each sub-topic from 0 to 5, asks one question at a time, schedules spaced review and ends with a final assessment. It uses the common SKILL.md format, so it works in Claude Code and other agents that load skills.
skill_of_week.note: It gained about 7,700 stars this week, mostly after a Hacker News post with 649 points. The repo has one skill and only two commits, with no tests or stated maintenance plan. It is a single prompt file under the MIT license, so it costs only the model tokens of each session. It teaches through questions, so it is slow by design: use it to learn a topic, not to get a fast answer.
